correctness.rationale: Published 2026 outer-extremizer theorem for every bounded H^p functional with p<1 makes any maximizer zero-free and outer; take analytic fourth root g in H2, norm1. Coefficients of g^4 give |a0+tau a2|<=x²+4tau x^(3/2)sqrt(v)+6tau x(1-x-v), where x=|g0|²,v=|g2|², |g1|²=1-x-v, tails waste H2 norm. Exact v optimization gives v=x/9 if x<=9/10 and v=1-x if x>=9/10; a one-variable calculus step yields tau=1/2 change of extremizer family and N(tau) piecewise. Independently verified SymPy N(1/2)=27/20, N''(left)=81/125 and N''(right)=486/125. Phase equality gives unique even fourth power for tau<=1/2 and two conjugate-sign linear-term fourth powers for tau>1/2; both outer by root moduli. Supporting-line duality identifies Phi2 for t>=81/256 and terminal Phi2=Phi1 for t>=81/100 using published Theorem12(ii). Finite checker is corroboration, not H^p outer theorem proof.
residual_risks: Outer-extremizer theorem is an external published premise, not independently reproved. No fixed-origin frontier asserted for t<81/256.

evidence: Pure a2 coefficient bound and high-origin first coefficient theorem broadly cover two limiting/corollary quantities, not full tau transition.
